title.narrative: Financial Market Development And Inclusion Program - Subprogram 3

description.narrative: The program supports the main reform priorities of the government and the Financial Services Authority (OJK) to further develop and make the finance sector more inclusive by (i) strengthening the regulatory structure for financial stability, (ii) deepening the financial market, and (iii) enhancing financial inclusion.

description.narrative: Development and inclusiveness of the finance sector increased
Size of finance sector as percentage of gross domestic product increased by 20%. (2014 baseline: 103%) Data Source: ADB Key Statistics and Asian Bonds Online Actual value:
Access to financial services for the 40% poorest increased to 40%. (2014 baseline: 21.9%) Data Source: FINDEX Global Database Actual value:
Reduction in 5-year credit default swap spreads by 30 basis points. (2013-2015 baseline average: 176.1 basis points) Data Source: Asian Bonds Online Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Financial inclusion enhanced Indicator: Branchless banking expansion approved to cover 29 banks and more than 800,000 agents. 2017 baseline: 16 banks and 106,490 agents). Data Source: OJK's website Actual value:

Output: Finance sector deepened Indicator: OJK implemented all IFSB standards for capital market and Takaful and 67% of IFSB standards for banking. (2017 baseline: 50% of standards implemented) Data Source: IFSB annual survey Actual value:

Output: Regulatory structure for financial stability strengthened Indicator: OJK implemented 90% of priority reform actions and 83% of other actions in the consolidated finance sector master plan. (2017 baseline: OJK implemented 17% of priority reform action) Data Source: OJK's quarterly report Actual value:

Output: Finance sector deepened Indicator: Municipal bond financing plan and detailed list of projects, including hospital wings for mothers and children, approved by the local government of Central Java. (2017 baseline: No financing plan and no detailed list of projects for municipal financing available) Data Source: Report from local government of Central Java Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: Financial inclusion enhanced Indicator: National Council for Financial Inclusion is fully operational with seven working groups, including financial literacy and consumer protection. (2017 baseline: National Council for Financial Inclusion set up) Data Source: Website and quarterly reports of National Council for Financial Inclusion Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: Financial inclusion enhanced Indicator: OJK implemented 40 financial literacy programs, including three dedicated for women. (2017 baseline: Three outreach programs including one for women) Data Source: OJK's financial literacy reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: Regulatory structure for financial stability strengthened Indicator: Regulation to regulate financial holding companies prepared by OJK (2017 baseline: No regulation on financial holding companies) Data Source: OJK's Annual Report Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y
